html:
In 1739 the British in Jamaica signed peace treaties with the Maroons, communities of escaped Africans in the mountains, after decades of war. The Maroons kept their freedom and land.

Maroon bands had formed when the Spanish fled the English invasion of 1655 and grew as more people escaped the sugar estates. Under leaders such as Cudjoe in the west and Queen Nanny in the Blue Mountains, they beat British forces in the First Maroon War.

The price of peace was that the Maroons would return future runaways and help put down revolts, as they did in Tacky's Revolt. Maroon towns such as Accompong and Moore Town still keep their own customs and treaty rights. Nanny is a National Hero of Jamaica.
sum: In 1739 the British in Jamaica signed peace treaties with the Maroons, communities of escaped Africans in the mountains, after decades of war. The Maroons kept their freedom and land.
